method: Independent clean-room audit of the current rewrite only, starting with AGENTS.md. Fully read all 115 original deployment/release assignment files, then all 54 reassigned Web test files, including fixture setup, async control flow, assertions, and failure paths rather than test names alone. Reread any truncated output. Fully read four current Web implementation files to cross-check operation receipts, terminal identity, authentication generations, draft acknowledgement and history merging. Reviewed the entire dependency lock and capability inventory using the explicitly described all-entry structural and semantic method. No previous audit conclusions, remediation reports, old repository code, Git history or another reviewer conclusion were used. Only four exact targeted test files ran with local pure-data or browser-storage substitutes; no aggregate test selection or live integration ran.

dependencyLock.method: Read every nonblank semantic line, including importers, versions, engines, platform restrictions, optional dependencies, peer dependencies and every snapshot dependency edge. The 336 repetitive integrity strings were not individually visually compared; every resolution line was programmatically required to contain the canonical sha512 Base64 structure and decode to 64 bytes. No remote artifact download or vulnerability-database claim is made.

capabilityInventory.method: Parsed the complete JSON, then fully read every method, evidence group, additional workflow and metadata entry with only sha256/reportSha256 values elided from the semantic view. Independently checked every unique referenced path/hash pair against current bytes. Historical audit/report references were checked only for existence and hash, without reading their contents or conclusions. Inventory coverage claims were treated as source assertions, not inherited audit conclusions.

validations.scope: Python pure-data and temporary-file cases: lock byte cap, growth, encoding, descriptor closure and replacement/mutation checks; current ledger DDL recovery states and incompatible-schema no-mutation behavior. Used the authorized Python runtime and task-local temporary directory.

Local browser-storage and transport substitutes plus pure history transformations. Checked independent intents, monotonic accepted facts, acknowledgement tombstones, corrupt-storage dispatch blocking, terminal connection/operation identity and history reconciliation. No real browser account, process, model or external service was used.

reviewFocus: Deployment identity and authority separation, root-owned checkout admission, sanitized build inputs, offline build boundaries, archive limits, fixed privileged verbs, launcher process/environment/descriptor isolation and provider host fingerprints.

Install, update, rollback, HTTPS and provider transactions: quiescence before publication, staged control-plane imports, active/enabled service restoration, current edge preservation, native journal migration and positive-witness limits.

Workspace file descriptors, no-replace/revision checks, recovery material, Git raw-byte views, index/commit leases, worktree archive/restore and durable spool receipts versus staging or native completion logs.

Release scanner behavior, exact affected-test selection, CI platform/fixture boundaries, clean audit gating, docs and ordinary feature-evidence consistency without treating historic results as current execution.

All Web test bodies: explicit action and consent, unknown outcome recovery without replay, immutable identity and connection ownership, A-to-B-to-A generation changes, late results, preserved draft revisions, private-data lifetime, bounded media/logs, complete history and precise file/Git revisions.
limitations: Complete means all 169 assigned files and four declared supplementary files were inspected. It is not a claim that this reviewer alone inspected all 1788 repository files or independently executed every capability represented by the inventory.

The dependency-lock integrity review validated structure and decoded size, not remote package bytes or current upstream vulnerability status. The capability-reference hash review proves byte agreement and existence, not correctness of historical conclusions.
All assigned deployment probes and Web test sources were read, but only the four exact targeted files listed under validations were executed. No other test outcomes are claimed for this review.

No full or aggregate test suite, build, release scanner run, Git history inspection, SSH, deployment, privileged host action, real systemd/cgroup operation, external MCP, paid model call, personal runtime home, real media capture, real PTY or remote environment was exercised.

Linux ownership, kernel isolation, live service transaction recovery and actual browser/media behavior remain static-review boundaries here; substitute tests and ordinary feature evidence are not new production validation.

No product code, test, documentation or ordinary feature-evidence file was changed. Only ignored task work files and this reviewer report were written. The post-write snapshot and report SHA are returned separately after the final write.
